title: Variation along a graph walk
statement: Let $G$ be a regular multigraph of degree $D$, let $F$ assign a rational number to each vertex, and let $a$ be rational. Suppose that for every vertex $x$ and every index $i$ among the $D$ neighbor indices, $|F(x)-F(G.	ext{nbr}(x,i))|\le a$. For any vertex $t$ and any walk $p$ from $x$ to $t$ in the graph whose edges join adjacent vertices of $G$, one has $|F(x)-F(t)|\le \operatorname{length}(p)\,a$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is finite and has decidable equality
$G$ is a regular multigraph of degree $D$
For every vertex $x$ and neighbor index $i$, $|F(x)-F(G.\text{nbr}(x,i))|\le a$
$p$ is a walk from $x$ to $t$ in the graph induced by adjacency in $G$
